parts.title: Task 1 · Long reading: choose a title
parts.instruction: Read the article. There are six titles (a-f) and five paragraphs, numbered [1] to [5]. For questions 1-5, choose the best title for each paragraph. Each title can be used only once; one title is not needed. Reading and Writing together take 2 hours; Task 1 should take about 20 minutes.

texts.label: Article
texts.title: Second life for old bicycles
paras: [1] Three years ago, Priya Nair noticed a pile of broken bicycles behind a block of flats in Stockport. Nobody wanted them, and the council planned to take them to the tip. Priya, who was a primary school teacher at the time, asked if she could have them instead. She paid £40 for a van and moved the bikes into an empty garage that belonged to her uncle.

[2] At first she only wanted to repair a few bikes for the children in her street. She watched videos online and borrowed tools from her neighbours. Within a month, other people began to bring their own bikes, and a retired mechanic called Tom Ellery offered to help. By the end of the year the garage was open every Saturday morning, and about 30 people came each week.

[3] Today the Bike Shed has twelve volunteers and a small shop at the front. A repaired bike in the shop costs between £30 and £90, but the repair sessions are free. Anyone can bring in a bike and learn to fix it with a volunteer's help. 'I never tell people what to do,' says Tom. 'I show them once, and then they do it themselves. That is the only way to learn.'

[4] The project helps more than just cyclists. A local college sends students there for work experience, and two of them have since found jobs in bike shops. The Bike Shed also gives away around 150 bikes a year to families who cannot afford one. The money from sales pays for the rent and new parts, although Priya admits that there is rarely anything left at the end of the month.

[5] Last winter the roof of the garage leaked, and the volunteers had to close for three weeks. After that, the group decided that it needed a better home. This autumn the Bike Shed is moving to a larger building next to the railway station, which the council is renting to the group at a low price. Priya hopes to open a second workshop for electric bikes by next summer. She has also given up teaching to work at the Bike Shed full time.

items.prompt: Which title fits paragraph [1]?
items.why: The paragraph is about the broken bikes that the council wanted to take to the tip, and Priya rescuing them.

items.prompt: Which title fits paragraph [2]?
items.why: Priya starts with a few bikes for local children; within a year about 30 people come each week.

items.prompt: Which title fits paragraph [3]?
items.why: Free repair sessions where people learn to fix their own bikes; Tom says 'they do it themselves'.

items.prompt: Which title fits paragraph [4]?
items.why: Work experience for students and free bikes for families: help that goes beyond cycling.

items.prompt: Which title fits paragraph [5]?
items.why: After the leaking roof, the group is moving to a larger building. Bicycle prices (d) are not mentioned.

parts.title: Task 2 · Multi-text reading: which text?
parts.instruction: Read the four texts, A-D, about travelling to work. For questions 19-23, choose the text (A, B, C or D) that matches each statement. You can use a text more than once. Task 2 should take about 20 minutes.

texts.label: Text A
texts.title: Rosa's blog: Two wheels to work
paras: I have cycled to my office in Bristol for two years now. The journey is 6 miles and takes me about 35 minutes, which is quicker than the bus at rush hour. My company has showers and a locked room for bikes, so I arrive fresh. The only problem is winter. Last December I nearly gave up because of the dark mornings, so I bought good lights and a waterproof coat. Now I save about £60 a month on bus tickets and I feel much healthier. My advice is to start with two days a week.

texts.label: Text B
texts.title: Newspaper: Night bus for hospital staff
paras: From 3 November a new bus, the N7, will run between Wexford Road and the County Hospital every night. Buses will leave every 30 minutes between 10 pm and 5 am. Until now, nurses and cleaners who finish late have had to take taxis or ask friends for a lift. A single ticket on the N7 will cost £2, but hospital staff can travel for £1 if they show their work card. The service will be tested for six months, and then the bus company will decide whether to keep it.

texts.label: Text C
texts.title: Email from Hamid, Facilities Manager: Car park changes
paras: Dear all,

From 1 March the staff car park will have 40 spaces instead of 80, because the building next door is being extended. Employees who travel to work in one car with at least two colleagues will have priority for a space. If you would like to find people to share with, please add your name to the list at reception.
Anyone who comes by train can claim up to £20 a month towards the cost of a season ticket.
Thanks, Hamid

texts.label: Text D
texts.title: Kenji on a work-from-home forum
paras: My employer moved to a hybrid system last year, so I go to the office only on Tuesdays and Thursdays. I drive, because the train from my village runs only once an hour, and the journey takes 45 minutes each way. On the other three days I work from my kitchen table. I do miss chatting with colleagues, and my flat is small, so I am thinking of renting a desk in a shared workspace near my home. It costs £120 a month.

items.prompt: Which writer says they miss talking to colleagues?
items.why: Kenji: 'I do miss chatting with colleagues'.

items.prompt: Which text is about people who finish work late at night?
items.why: The N7 is for nurses and cleaners 'who finish late'.

items.prompt: Which text offers help with the cost of a train season ticket?
items.why: Hamid: staff can claim up to £20 a month towards a season ticket.

items.prompt: Which writer saves money by changing the way they travel?
items.why: Rosa saves about £60 a month on bus tickets.

items.prompt: Which text says that fewer people will be able to park?
items.why: The car park goes from 80 spaces to 40.

parts.title: Task 3 · Reading into writing
parts.instruction: You have about 40 minutes. In the exam you answer a question in three parts, using information from all four Task 2 texts. Use your own words; do not copy whole sentences from the texts. Write 100-130 words.

tasks.title: Getting to work: an email to a friend
tasks.situation:
Your friend Jess has a new job 8 miles from her home and asks you for ideas about how to get there. You have read four texts on travelling to work.
Text A, Rosa's blog: she cycles 6 miles to her office in Bristol in about 35 minutes, which is quicker than the bus at rush hour. Her company has showers and a locked room for bikes. She saves about £60 a month, but needed good lights and a waterproof coat for dark winter mornings.
Text B, newspaper: from 3 November a new night bus, the N7, runs every 30 minutes between 10 pm and 5 am from Wexford Road to the County Hospital. A single ticket costs £2 (£1 for hospital staff). It will be tested for six months.
Text C, email from Hamid: the staff car park will have 40 spaces instead of 80. People who share a car with at least two colleagues get priority; people who come by train can claim up to £20 a month towards a season ticket.
Text D, Kenji's forum post: he works at the office two days a week and drives 45 minutes each way, because the train from his village runs only once an hour. He works at his kitchen table on the other days, misses his colleagues and is thinking of renting a desk in a shared workspace for £120 a month.
tasks.prompt: Write an email to Jess (100-130 words). Use information from all four texts, in your own words, to answer these three questions:
points: What different ways of getting to work do the texts describe?
What are the advantages and disadvantages of two of them?
Which way would you suggest for Jess, and why?
tasks.model:
Hi Jess,

Congratulations on the new job! You could cycle, take a bus or train, or drive.

Cycling can be quick and cheap. One woman in Bristol rides six miles in about 35 minutes and saves around £60 a month. However, she needed good lights and a waterproof coat for dark winter mornings. Driving is easy if public transport is poor, but a man in a village spends 45 minutes on the road each way, and some companies are reducing their parking spaces.

I would suggest cycling two or three days a week, if your office has showers. On the other days you could share a car with a colleague, which gives you a better chance of finding a parking space.

Speak soon,
Alex
checklist: All three questions answered: ways of travelling, advantages and disadvantages of two, a suggestion with a reason
Information taken from all four texts (A bike, B bus, C car park and train, D driving and home working)
Your own words: no sentences copied from the texts
Email layout: greeting, short opening, paragraphs, friendly ending
100-130 words; linking words such as however, but, because, so

parts.title: Task 4 · Extended writing
parts.instruction: You have about 40 minutes. In the exam you choose one of several tasks, for example an email, an article, a story, a review or an essay. Write 100-130 words.

tasks.title: Article: A trip I will never forget
tasks.situation: An English-language website for learners is asking readers to send in short articles with the title 'A trip I will never forget'.
points: where you went and who you went with
what you had planned to do
why you will never forget the trip
tasks.model:
A trip I will never forget

Last summer, my cousin Leila and I took a train to the coast for the day. We had planned everything: sandwiches, sun cream and a map of the beach. Unfortunately, we got on the wrong train and ended up in a small town two hours away from where we wanted to be.

At first we were annoyed, but then a friendly woman at the station told us about a market near the river. We spent the afternoon eating fresh bread, listening to a street band and chatting to local people. In the evening we finally reached the sea, just in time to watch the sunset.

I will never forget that day because it showed me that mistakes can lead to wonderful surprises.
checklist: A title and a clear beginning, middle and end
All four points covered
Past tenses used correctly (past simple for events, past perfect or 'had planned' for earlier plans)
Linking words: at first, but, then, in the evening, because
100-130 words; a few interesting details, not just a list

parts.title: Independent listening · Talk 1
parts.instruction: You will hear a talk by a woman about a weekend away. You hear it twice. In the exam you answer six questions aloud; here, type a short answer for questions 1-6. In the exam, listening and speaking together take about 18 minutes.

script.t: Hi everyone, and thanks for coming to the club tonight. I'd like to tell you about a walking weekend I had last month in the Lake District. I went with my sister, Anna, and we travelled by train from Manchester, which took just under two hours. We had planned to stay in a hostel, but it was full, so we found a small bed and breakfast in a village called Grasmere instead. It cost seventy pounds a night for the two of us, and the owner, a lovely man called Colin, gave us a huge breakfast every morning.

On Saturday we walked up a hill called Helm Crag. It was only about four miles, but it was very steep, and it started to rain halfway up. We were soaked, but the view from the top was wonderful. On Sunday we were more careful and chose an easy walk around the lake. That afternoon we visited a little museum about a famous poet, and then we caught the five o'clock train home.

The best thing was the quiet. I didn't use my phone once, because there was almost no signal! Next time, I'd like to go in autumn, when the colours are beautiful. Anna wants to try camping, but I'm not sure. I like a proper bed.

items.prompt: Marisol and Anna travelled from Manchester by ____.
items.why: 'we travelled by train from Manchester'.

items.prompt: What was the name of the village where they stayed?
items.why: 'a village called Grasmere'.

items.prompt: How much did the room cost for one night?
items.why: 'It cost seventy pounds a night for the two of us'.

items.prompt: What started halfway up the hill on Saturday?
items.why: 'it started to rain halfway up'.

items.prompt: What did they visit on Sunday afternoon?
items.why: 'we visited a little museum about a famous poet'.

items.prompt: Why did Marisol not use her phone?
items.why: 'because there was almost no signal'.

parts.title: Independent listening · Talk 2
parts.instruction: You will hear a man giving a talk. Listen once and choose what the talk is about (question 7). Then listen again and type a short answer for questions 8-13. (In the exam you say this aloud, and there are four more questions that are not included here.)

script.t: Good evening. My name's Daniel, and I'd like to tell you why I started learning Spanish two years ago. I'm an engineer, and my company has an office in Madrid. Every few months they asked me to go there, and I could only say hello and thank you, which was embarrassing. So I joined an evening class at the local college. It meets every Wednesday for two hours, and there are twelve students in my group.

Our teacher, Lucia, comes from Seville, and she makes the lessons fun. We play games and talk about films rather than just doing grammar exercises. Honestly, the hardest part for me is listening, because Spanish people speak so fast! To practise, I watch a Spanish series for half an hour every evening, with the subtitles on. I also have a language partner, Javier, who lives in Madrid. We video-call on Sundays. He helps me with my Spanish and I help him with his English.

Last month I went to Madrid again and, for the first time, I ordered a whole meal in Spanish. The waiter even said my accent was good, which made me very proud. In the summer I'm taking the exam for level B1, and then I want to try Italian, but my wife says I should learn to cook first!

items.question: First listening: what is the talk about?
options: A man explains why and how he is learning a language.
A man describes a business trip to Spain.
A teacher gives advice on how to teach grammar.
A man talks about moving to a new country.
items.why: Daniel talks about his Spanish class and how he practises. The trips to Madrid are only a small part of it.

items.prompt: What is Daniel's job?
items.why: 'I'm an engineer'.

items.prompt: How many students are in his group?
items.why: 'there are twelve students in my group'.

items.prompt: Which city does his teacher come from?
items.why: 'Our teacher, Lucia, comes from Seville'.

items.prompt: What is the hardest part of learning Spanish for him?
items.why: 'the hardest part for me is listening'.

items.prompt: On which day of the week does he video-call Javier?
items.why: 'We video-call on Sundays'.

items.why: 'I'm taking the exam for level B1'.

parts.title: Topic
parts.instruction: In the exam you prepare one topic before the day and bring a topic form with a title and four points. You talk about it with the examiner for up to 4 minutes, and you ask the examiner at least one question. Prepare the sample topic below (about 10 minutes), then talk for 3-4 minutes. Record yourself or practise with a friend who plays the examiner.

tasks.situation: Your topic form says 'Learning to cook'. The examiner asks you to start. Use each point on your form, give reasons and examples, and ask the examiner a question about the topic at some point.

card.title: Topic form: Learning to cook
lines: 2. What I want to learn to cook next (future and intention)
3. Why I enjoy cooking, or why I do not (reasons and opinions)
4. Will more people cook at home in ten years? (predicting and certainty)

redemittel: I'm going to learn how to ...
I'm sure that ... / I think it's likely that ...
What about you? Do you cook at home?
tasks.model:
Candidate: Hello. My topic is learning to cook. First, I'll tell you what I cooked recently. Last Sunday I made a vegetable curry for my family. It was the first time I used fresh spices, and my brother said it was better than the one from our favourite takeaway!
Examiner: That sounds good. What would you like to learn next?
Candidate: I'm going to learn how to bake bread. I've just bought a book about it, and I'd like to try it this weekend. It looks difficult, but I think it will be worth it.
Examiner: Why do you enjoy cooking?
Candidate: Mainly because it helps me relax after work. I also prefer home cooking to ready meals, because it's cheaper and healthier. Do you cook at home?
Examiner: Sometimes, yes. Do you think more people will cook at home in the future?
Candidate: I'm sure they will. Food in shops is getting more expensive, and there are lots of videos online that show how to cook simple meals. So I think it's likely that many people will learn.
checklist: All four points from the form covered, in a sensible order
Past (recent) and future/intention structures used correctly: 'I made', 'I've just bought', 'I'm going to ...'
Reasons and opinions given with 'because', 'I prefer', 'in my opinion'
A prediction with a certainty word: 'I'm sure', 'I think it's likely'
At least one question asked to the examiner
Clear pronunciation and a steady pace; you kept going without long silences

parts.title: Conversation
parts.instruction: In the exam the examiner chooses one subject area (travel, money, fashion, rules and regulations, health and fitness, or learning a foreign language) and talks with you for about 2 minutes. You do not prepare. Answer the sample questions below aloud, then ask one question of your own.

tasks.situation: Subject area: Travel. The examiner asks you some questions and expects you to answer fully, give reasons and ask a question back.

card.title: Subject area: Travel
lines: Where did you go on your last trip?
Do you prefer travelling by train or by plane? Why?
Where are you going to travel to next?
What do you think is the most important thing to take on holiday?
Ask the examiner: What do you think about travelling alone?

redemittel: The last time I travelled, I went to ...
I think it's essential to take ...
What do you think about ...? / Have you ever ...?
tasks.model:
Examiner: Where did you go on your last trip?
Candidate: Last month I went to Lisbon with two friends. We stayed for four days, and we walked everywhere.
Examiner: Do you prefer travelling by train or by plane?
Candidate: I prefer the train, because you can look out of the window and there is more space. But for long distances the plane is quicker, so it depends on how much time I have.
Examiner: Where are you going to travel to next?
Candidate: I'm hoping to visit Scotland next summer. I'd like to go walking in the mountains.
Examiner: What is the most important thing to take on holiday?
Candidate: I think it's essential to take a good pair of shoes. Then you can enjoy the day without sore feet. What do you think about travelling alone?
Examiner: I like it sometimes, because you can do what you want.
checklist: Answers of two or three sentences, not just one word
Reasons given with 'because' and a preference with 'I prefer'
Past tense for the last trip, future or intention for the next one
One question asked back to the examiner
Natural reactions and no long pauses
